extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern visual science attributes motion perception primarily to the beta movement and phi phenomenon processed in the visual cortex.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Persistence of vision alone explains why the human brain perceives sequential still drawings as smooth, continuous motion.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pioneers like Emile Cohl and Winsor McCay produced hand-drawn animated films decades before Steamboat Willie popularized synced sound.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Walt Disney invented the first animated cartoon when his studio released Steamboat Willie with synchronized sound in 1928.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Animation requires manipulating each frame individually between exposures rather than capturing continuous real-time motion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Live-action video recorded at 24 frames per second is a form of animation because it displays sequential still frames.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Animating on twos means holding each single drawing for two consecutive frames, requiring only 12 drawings per second of film.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Animating on twos means drawing two completely different pictures for every single frame of a 24-frame-per-second film.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the illusion of continuous motion when the playback frame rate drops below ten frames per second?
Which mechanical difference separates a spinning zoetrope drum from a multi-plane camera setup in early studio history?
What frame-count measurement on an exposure sheet confirms how long a held pose stays on screen at 24 frames per second?
Where should a Scout position light sources when photographing cel layers or flipbooks to prevent glare and eye strain?

extra_misconceptions.fact: An object must maintain a constant overall volume, getting wider only as it compresses vertically upon impact.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Squash and stretch means expanding both the height and width of an object at the exact same moment of impact.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A trailing cape is follow through and overlapping action, whereas secondary action is a deliberate gesture supporting the main act.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Secondary action is the same principle as overlapping action when a character's cape trails behind a jump.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Placing more frames closely around a key pose slows the motion down, creating a smooth slow-in or slow-out effect.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding more in-between frames around a pose speeds up the movement across that section of the timeline.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Almost all organic appendages pivot around joints, causing hands, feet, and heads to travel along curved circular arcs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mechanical limbs and natural human joints naturally follow straight linear paths between two key poses.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the perceived mass of a bouncing ball if its overall volume changes during squash and stretch?
Under what condition does straight ahead action work better than pose to pose keyframes in a character scene?
What frame-spacing measurement between key poses confirms that a pendulum swing uses slow in and slow out?
Why is it dangerous to act out high-impact reference poses without clearing floor hazards around your workspace first?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thumbnails are small, rapid rough drawings used strictly to plan staging, camera angles, and major pose flow before production.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Thumbnail sketches must be fully shaded, high-detail illustrations before a Scout begins animating the final scene.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Auto-exposure and auto-focus cause distracting brightness flicker and focus breathing whenever the animator's hand enters the frame.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Automatic camera exposure and auto-focus settings improve consistency during a stop-motion claymation shoot.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Digital software only interpolates math between keyframes; the animator must still plan timing, weight, and poses by hand.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Three-dimensional computer animation software builds believable character movement automatically without human planning.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sharp repetitive bends snap aluminum armature wire quickly, so animators distribute curves gently along the joint span.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stop-motion armatures can be bent repeatedly at sharp ninety-degree angles without fatiguing the internal wire skeleton.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a stop-motion scene when the camera tripod or table shifts by two millimeters mid-shot?
Which visual indicator in onion-skinning software distinguishes previous frames from upcoming key drawings?
What timing log on a storyboard or dope sheet confirms that dialogue or sound effects match your key poses?
Why is it dangerous to leave hot studio lamps or loose power cords unsecured around a stop-motion stage?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Industries rely on animation every day for surgical rehearsal, architectural walkthroughs, flight simulators, and accident reconstruction.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Professional animation studios use animation exclusively to produce entertainment cartoons, movies, and video games.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Studio production pipelines divide work across specialized departments including storyboarding, rigging, layout, animation, and lighting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: One individual animator in a commercial studio typically models, rigs, lights, animates, and renders an entire feature film.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Technical and medical animations must obey strict physical dimensions and telemetry data so doctors and engineers make accurate decisions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scientific and engineering visualizations use the same squash-and-stretch exaggeration rules as Saturday morning cartoons.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unreleased storyboards, character designs, and proprietary tools are protected intellectual property covered by strict studio NDAs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Photographing artist monitors during a studio tour is harmless because unfinished wireframes have no commercial value.

extra_socratic_questions: Which pipeline stage during a studio tour converts raw 3D geometry and lighting data into final viewable frames?
What happens to a forensic or medical simulation if the animator prioritizes dramatic exaggeration over physics?
What latency or frame-rate metric confirms that a virtual reality training simulation will not cause motion sickness?
Where should a visitor stand and what rules apply regarding unreleased screens during an in-person studio tour?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Recruiters evaluate candidates primarily on the quality of their short demo reel, acting choices, and mastery of animation principles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-year university degree in fine arts automatically guarantees an entry-level job as a studio character animator.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Riggers build the digital skeleton, joints, and control handles, while animators use those controls to pose and move the character.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Character riggers and character animators perform the exact same daily tasks inside a 3D animation pipeline.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hiring directors prefer a tight 45-to-60-second demo reel showing only the applicant's strongest, fully polished shots first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A longer demo reel containing every student exercise is always more impressive to a studio hiring director.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Roles like technical director, 3D rigger, simulation artist, and render wrangler require programming, math, and physics skills instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in an animation studio requires fast freehand drawing skills with paper and pencil.

extra_socratic_questions: Which technical responsibility separates a character rigger from a character animator on a 3D production team?
What happens to an entry-level job application if a candidate submits a four-minute demo reel with weak early clips?
What ergonomic desk and wrist posture adjustments prevent repetitive strain injuries during long studio shifts?
Which specific breakdown notes in a demo reel log confirm which shots a candidate animated versus modeled or lit?
